project: Customer Writing Standard and Terminology Register
description: Implement the documentation-only foundation from Story 1 of the Customer Prose Standard and Enforcement Plan: publish an indexed normative customer technical-writing standard, a versioned and parseable YAML product terminology register, and a manual language-review checklist. The project gives authors and reviewers one contract for labels, procedures, descriptions, product terms, protected technical text, examples, exceptions, and ASD-STE100-aligned conformance language, without implementing prosecheck or rewriting the existing corpus.

context.customerAsk: Implement Story 1 of docs/internal/development/plans/customer-prose-standard-and-enforcement.md exactly within the documentation-only lane: add the normative customer technical-writing standard under docs/internal/standards/writing/, add the YAML terminology register, index the standard from docs/internal/standards/STANDARDS.md, and provide the required manual review checklist.
context.problem: Five downstream prose and documentation plans are blocked because authors and reviewers have no normative repository writing contract, no structured product terminology register, and no explicit boundary between deterministic checks and human language review. Product vocabulary, technical-literal protection, exceptions, and conformance claims can therefore vary by reviewer or prior chat context.
context.solution: Publish one repository-specific writing profile defining content classes, protected technical text, deterministic and human-review boundaries, suppression policy, ASD-STE100-aligned conformance limits, examples, and a manual checklist. Publish a versioned YAML register with canonical terms, definitions, approved forms, discouraged alternatives, examples, valid surfaces, and ownership references. Connect the artifacts through the standards index and cross-links so downstream checker and migration work can consume one authoritative contract.

acceptanceCriteria: An author can use the normative standard to determine how to write a label, procedure, description, command or code example, product term, and justified exception without relying on chat history or reviewer preference.

The standard defines required content classes, protected machine and technical text, deterministic automated-rule boundaries, human-review rules, suppression policy, repository-specific good and bad examples, and the approved ASD-STE100 conformance claim.

The versioned terminology register parses as YAML using the documented schema, covers all required initial public nouns plus customer-visible relationship and lifecycle names, and limits internal Petri-net terms to explicitly internal or implementation-focused contexts.
Architecture and data-model owners confirm the terminology definitions and owning references, with blocking terminology feedback resolved before merge.

Authors and reviewers can discover the standard, terminology register, and manual checklist from the standards index; Markdown renders legibly and document links resolve to the intended repository sources.
Typecheck and applicable docs-only tests pass; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared-file changes are resolved against current main, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Authors can apply one normative writing contract
userStories.description: As an author, I want one repository writing standard for customer-facing prose so I can write clear labels, instructions, explanations, examples, and exceptions without depending on reviewer preference.
acceptanceCriteria: The standard separately defines labels, procedural prose, descriptive prose, machine and technical text, and technical terms, including when each class applies.

Procedural rules require no more than 20 words per sentence, one instruction per sentence unless actions must occur simultaneously, an imperative verb, necessary conditions before the instruction, an observable expected result, and an ordered or vertical list when sequence matters.

Descriptive rules require no more than 25 words per sentence, gradual introduction of information, one topic per paragraph, no more than six sentences per paragraph, preferred active voice, and stable key words or phrases for related information.

Protected-text guidance covers code fences, inline code, commands and shell operators, JSON and YAML contract examples, API methods and routes, paths, URLs, package paths, identifiers, schema, event, status and error-code literals, model and provider names, quoted external output, and generated artifacts; safely identifiable natural-language comments remain reviewable.

The standard distinguishes blocking deterministic rules, advisory rules, and human-review rules using the governing plan's rule sets, and defines bounded rule-specific suppressions with reasons while rejecting suppressions for ordinary readability debt.

The standard says the repository profile is aligned with ASD-STE100, does not redistribute its controlled dictionary, does not claim checker certification or full ASD-STE100 conformance, and names the documented review, training, and dictionary conditions required before a stronger claim.
Repository-specific paired good and bad examples cover at least a command description, procedure, explanation, product term, protected technical example, and valid or invalid exception.
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Implemented the normative customer technical-writing standard at docs/internal/standards/writing/customer-technical-writing-standard.md. It defines labels, procedures, descriptions, machine and technical text, technical terms, the protected-literal boundary, blocking/advisory/human review rules, bounded rule-specific exceptions, ASD-STE100-aligned claim limits, paired repository examples, and the manual review checklist. `git diff --cached --check` passed before commit. An initial make typecheck run reached TypeScript but was blocked by pre-existing Assertion.not errors in untouched UI test helpers; the repository-wide rerun during Story 002 passed after dependencies were restored. No UI or runtime files changed in this story. Stories 002 and 003 remain open.

userStories.title: Maintainers can consume the product terminology register as structured data
userStories.description: As an author or future tooling maintainer, I want a versioned, parseable product terminology register so public nouns stay consistent and internal implementation vocabulary does not leak into customer prose.
acceptanceCriteria: The YAML document has a top-level integer version set to 1 and a top-level terms sequence; every term record uses the same documented field schema.

Each term record contains non-empty canonical, definition, category, approvedForms, discouragedAlternatives, example, surfaces, and owner fields. approvedForms explicitly represents applicable plural or verb forms, and each discouraged alternative records its text, whether it is discouraged or prohibited, and the approved replacement.

category values are limited to product-term, technical-noun, technical-verb, acronym, command, or protected-literal; surfaces is a non-empty sequence that states where the term is valid; owner points to the architecture or contract source that owns the meaning.

The register covers at least Factory, Factory Session, Current Factory, Work, Work Request, Worker, Worker Session, Workstation, Provider, Provider Session, Model, Recording, Factory Event, and the customer-visible relationship and lifecycle names defined by the current data model and public contracts.
CPN, place, transition, marking, and token are registered as internal terms whose surfaces permit use only in explicitly internal or implementation-focused material.

Definitions and capitalization agree with docs/architecture/data-model.md and the owning public contracts; architecture and data-model owners record approval or resolve blocking corrections in the PR.
A standard YAML parser loads the complete register without errors, and a reviewer can identify each required field without relying on comments or implicit conventions.
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Added docs/internal/standards/writing/customer-technical-terms.yaml with version: 1, an explicit term-record schema, and 59 consistently shaped records. The register covers the required public nouns, customer-visible relationship names and protected literals, durable and live lifecycle names, and CPN/place/transition/marking/token with internal-only surfaces. Every owner reference resolves to an existing architecture or public-contract source. PyYAML loaded the complete register successfully, verified the required fields, allowed categories, alternative-record shape, and internal-term surface restrictions; `git diff --check` passed before the implementation commit. Definitions remain tied to the recorded architecture and contract owners for review. `make typecheck` passed on 2026-08-10 after dependencies were restored. No UI or runtime files changed. Story 003 remains incomplete.

userStories.title: Reviewers can discover and apply the complete prose review contract
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want the writing standard, terminology register, and manual checklist connected through the standards index so I can evaluate prose consistently and direct authors to one authoritative source.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/internal/standards/STANDARDS.md lists the customer technical-writing standard as the normative entry point and identifies when authors and reviewers must use it.

The standard links to the terminology register, architecture data model, and official ASD-STE100 references used by the governing plan; the terminology register's ownership references identify the intended repository sources.

The manual checklist requires reviewers to confirm approved vocabulary and meaning, one subject or instruction per sentence, justified passive voice, logical single-topic paragraphs, preserved technical and contract meaning, examples matching shipped CLI and public schemas, and precise warnings, destructive instructions, and failure recovery.
The checklist makes clear which findings can be automated and which require language or subject-matter judgment, and it does not describe the future checker as already implemented.
The standard, examples, checklist, and index render as readable Markdown, and following their repository links reaches the intended standard, register, data-model, or external reference.
No code, prosecheck implementation, prose baseline, CI enforcement, generated artifact, CLI manifest change, or customer-corpus rewrite is included in this story.
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Connected the normative writing standard, versioned terminology register, and embedded manual review checklist from docs/internal/standards/STANDARDS.md. The standard now links directly to the register, architecture data model, and official ASD-STE100 references; the checklist explicitly covers vocabulary and meaning, one subject or instruction per sentence, justified passive voice, single-topic paragraphs, technical and contract meaning, shipped CLI/public-schema examples, warnings, destructive instructions, failure recovery, exceptions, and the deterministic-versus-human review boundary. No checker, baseline, CI enforcement, generated artifact, CLI manifest change, or customer-corpus rewrite was added. `make typecheck` passed on 2026-08-10.
